title: Epic: Creep status effect engine
description: Runtime foundation for timed effects on creeps: chill/slow, poison damage over time, stun, armor break. Today towers can only subtract health, which is why splash and single-target feel identical apart from numbers. This epic delivers the pure effect model plus its game-loop integration, with no tower content attached - content lands in the tower archetype epic.
design: Effect state lives on the creep entity as a small fixed-shape list. Pure helpers (apply/tick/expire) live in entities/creep; the Phaser combat runtime only drives them with delta time. No per-frame allocations in the tick path.
acceptance_criteria: Effects apply, stack, tick and expire deterministically outside React; movement respects slow and stun; damage respects armor and armor break; damage over time grants kill rewards exactly once; the model is unit-tested without Phaser; frame budget holds with many affected creeps.

title: Define effect ids, magnitudes and stacking rules
description: Add the effect vocabulary to shared/types/content-ids: chill (movement slow), poison (damage over time), burn (stronger short damage over time), stun (movement stop) and armor_break (defense reduction). Define EffectDefinition (magnitude, durationMs, tickIntervalMs, maxStacks, stacking rule: refresh, stack or strongest-wins) and centralise the balance numbers in shared/constants.
acceptance_criteria: Effect ids are a typed union like the existing content ids; every effect declares its stacking rule explicitly; no magic numbers outside the constants module; the type guard helper matches the existing isTowerTypeId style.

title: Add active effects to the creep entity with pure apply and tick helpers
description: Extend CreepEntity with an activeEffects list and implement pure helpers in entities/creep: applyEffectToCreep (honouring the stacking rule), tickCreepEffects (returns damage to apply and the effects that expired) and getEffectiveSpeedMultiplier. No Phaser imports, no mutation of inputs beyond the documented in-place contract used by the runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Helpers are covered by unit tests for refresh, stack-to-cap and strongest-wins; expiry is exact at the boundary; ticking is deterministic for a fixed delta sequence; damage is reported, never applied inside the helper.

title: Tick effects in the game loop and route damage over time through kill rewards
description: Drive tickCreepEffects from the Phaser combat runtime each frame, apply the reported damage through applyDamageToCreep, and make sure a creep killed by poison grants gold exactly once through the same handleCreepKill path as a direct hit. Damage numbers for ticks must be visually distinguishable from hits.
acceptance_criteria: A creep killed by damage over time awards gold once and plays the death sound once; effects stop ticking on dead and escaped creeps; pausing and speed changes do not double-tick; covered by a runtime test.

title: Apply slow and stun to creep movement
description: Make the movement runtime multiply step distance by the creep effective speed multiplier, with stun clamping it to zero and a floor on slow so a creep can never be frozen forever by chill alone. Keep the per-frame path free of allocations.
acceptance_criteria: A chilled creep visibly lags an unaffected one and still reaches the exit; stun stops movement and releases on expiry; the minimum slow floor is a named constant; movement runtime tests cover both.

title: Apply unit armor and armor break to incoming damage
description: Creature armor is authored but currently ignored: applyDamageToCreep subtracts raw damage. Introduce a damage calculation that reduces incoming damage by armor (with a documented formula and a minimum damage floor) and lets the armor_break effect temporarily lower it. Keep the reward and kill semantics unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: The formula is documented in the damage module and unit-tested at zero, low and high armor; armor break restores on expiry; existing damage tests are updated rather than deleted; balance simulation tests still pass.

title: Render effect feedback on affected creeps
description: Show which effects are on a creep: a dominant-effect tint (blue chill, green poison, orange burn, white stun) layered under the existing hit flash, plus small status pips above the sprite when several effects are active. The hit flash must restore the effect tint, not the base faction tint, while an effect is running.
acceptance_criteria: Tint priority is deterministic and defined in one place; hit flash restores the correct colour; pips do not tank frame rate with many creeps; a test covers the tint restore ordering.

title: Add effect sound hooks to the audio manager
description: Add sound ids for effect application (chill, poison, stun) to the audio type map and trigger them with throttling so a wave of applications does not stack into noise. Register the missing wav files in docs/SOUND_ASSET_LIST.md as pending assets and fall back silently until they exist.
acceptance_criteria: Missing audio files never throw; the throttle window is a named constant; the category volume rules from the existing audio manager still apply; covered by an audio manager test.

title: Add determinism and hot-path performance tests for effects
description: Add tests that lock in the two properties the effect engine must keep: identical results for the same delta sequence regardless of frame pacing, and no unbounded growth of the effect list. Include a coarse budget assertion for ticking a large creep set within a frame.
acceptance_criteria: A fixed seed and delta sequence yield byte-identical effect state across runs; the effect list is capped by maxStacks; the budget test states its threshold and runs in the node environment.

title: Epic: Data-driven creature stats
description: Replace tier-formula unit generation with authored JSON content per race, so every creature has hand-tuned numbers instead of a value derived from its tier. This makes race identity expressible in data: a bat can move twice as fast with half the health, an abomination can crawl with heavy armor. Content lives in src/content/units/<race>.json, is validated on load, and stays the single source of truth for wave generation, duel sends and the unit registry.
design: JSON files are bundled via resolveJsonModule and validated at module init, so no async loading enters the Phaser scene and determinism is preserved. Validation helpers are written to be reused by tower content later.
acceptance_criteria: All creature stats come from validated JSON content; no tier-formula generators remain in src/entities/unit/model/config; registry, wave generation and creep sending read the same content; invalid content fails fast with a descriptive error; schema and roster parity are covered by tests.

title: Define the creature content schema and TypeScript contract
description: Introduce the authored content format for creatures: src/content/units/<race>.json with schemaVersion, race and a units array carrying id, name, tier, health, speed, armor, damage, rewardGold, spriteKey and description. Add the matching UnitContentFile and UnitContentEntry types in entities/unit, and enable resolveJsonModule in tsconfig.app.json if it is not already on.
acceptance_criteria: Types compile under strict TS with no any; a sample race file type-checks against the contract; the numeric fields keep the same names the runtime already uses so nothing downstream has to be renamed; unit test asserts the shape of a fixture file.

title: Add a fail-fast loader and validator for creature content

Errors must name the file and the offending unit id. Keep the primitive validators generic so tower content can reuse them later.
acceptance_criteria: Each failure mode has a test with a fixture; valid content returns typed UnitConfig values; validation runs once at module init and never inside the game loop; error messages identify file and unit id.
close_reason: Shared content validators plus loadUnitContent with fail-fast errors naming file and unit id; 22 validation tests

title: Migrate the undead roster to authored stats
description: Move the eight undead units from config/undead.ts into src/content/units/undead.json and replace formula output with hand-tuned numbers that express each creature: skeletons cheap and fragile, ghouls fast with low health, crypt fiends armored, gargoyles fast fliers, abomination slow with high health, frost wyrm as the wave-six threat. Delete the undead tier helpers.
acceptance_criteria: undead.ts no longer computes stats; getUnitsByTier keeps working against content; existing undead tests pass or are updated; wave composition still produces playable waves at wave 1, 5 and 10.
close_reason: Undead roster authored in content/units/undead.json; tier formula removed; wave health within 4% of the old curve at waves 1-20

title: Migrate orc, human and elf rosters with distinct race identity
description: Move the remaining three rosters to JSON and give each race a recognisable stat profile instead of the shared curve: orcs tanky and slow with high damage, humans balanced with better armor, elves fast and fragile with low reward gold. Remove the per-race tier helper functions.
acceptance_criteria: No config file computes stats from tier; each race reads visibly different in a stat table; tests cover that every race has at least one unit per tier it declares; balance simulation tests still pass.
close_reason: Orc, human and elf rosters authored in content with distinct profiles; race identity tests added; wave health within 10% and speed shifted per race identity

title: Add creature traits: movement type, size class and armor type
description: Extend the creature contract with optional gameplay traits that content can express: moveType (ground or air), sizeClass (small, medium, large) and armorType (unarmored, light, heavy). Default them when absent so existing content stays valid. Wire moveType into targeting so future anti-air towers have something to read, and expose armorType for the damage model.
acceptance_criteria: Traits are validated like other fields; defaults are explicit constants, not literals scattered in code; targeting and damage read traits through typed accessors; tests cover default fallback and explicit values.

title: Read the unit registry from content and drop the formula generators
description: Point entities/unit/model/registry.ts at loadUnitContent() and delete the createXUnit factories and TIER_* constants from all four config files. The config modules either disappear or shrink to a thin re-export of the loaded content.
acceptance_criteria: No TIER_HEALTH_BASE style constants remain in src; resolveUnitConfigById, getUnitsByFaction and getAllUnitConfigs behave identically; wave generation, creep sending and the computer opponent are untouched by the change; full test suite green.
close_reason: Registry loads all four content files through loadUnitContent; per-race modules are thin slices; no tier formulas remain

title: Add content guard tests for roster coverage and balance bounds
description: Add guard tests that catch bad authoring before it reaches the scene: every UnitId in the type union has content, every race registry sendableCreepIds entry resolves, health/speed/damage stay inside sane bounds, and generateWaveUnits still yields between the declared minimum and maximum units for waves 1 through 20.
acceptance_criteria: Tests fail with a clear message when a unit is missing or a stat is out of range; they run in the node environment and take under a second.

title: Document the creature content authoring flow
description: Write docs/08-content-authoring.md covering where creature JSON lives, what each field means, the allowed ranges, how tiers feed the wave budget, and how to add a new creature end to end including its sprite key. Link it from AGENTS.md so agents read it before touching content.
acceptance_criteria: A new creature can be added by following the doc alone; the doc states which fields are balance-sensitive and which are cosmetic.

title: Lazy-load the Phaser game bundle

acceptance_criteria: Menu route loads without the Phaser chunk; entering a match loads it on demand with a loading state; build reports a separate chunk.

close_reason: All child tasks done: income paid, single wallet, creep state deduplicated

title: Wire payIncome into match lifecycle
description: payIncome() in src/entities/duel-match/model/lifecycle.ts is implemented and tested but never called at runtime. Decide payout trigger (wave end / round end / fixed interval per docs/07-duel-mode-expansion-plan.md) and call it from GameScene wave/duel runtime for both player and computer opponent. Emit income-updated / gold change events through the bridge so HUD reflects payouts.
acceptance_criteria: Observable: queue a creep send, finish the wave, gold visibly increases by income amount for both player and AI opponent; covered by a deterministic simulation test.

title: Unify player gold into single source of truth
description: GameScene.playerGold (towers, kill/wave rewards) and duelMatchState.player.gold (creep send costs) are independent wallets. HUD shows playerGold while sends debit duel gold (GameScene.ts ~1271-1330, mapCreepSendPanelToViewModel.ts). Make duelMatchState the owner of gold (or one adapter over it); all credits/debits go through it; remove the second wallet.
acceptance_criteria: Observable: buying a tower reduces creep-send affordability and vice versa; CreepSendPanel button disabled state always matches real balance; all 414+ existing tests still pass.
close_reason: playerGold is single source of truth; duel gold synced at send/payout boundaries; tests green

description: Creeps sent by the opponent are added to duelMatchState.player.battlefield.creeps (routeQueuedSendsToBattlefields) AND spawned separately as Phaser creeps via getAdditionalWaveUnits. Leaks are only counted on Phaser creeps, so the duel battlefield list grows unbounded. Pick one owner for creep state and sync/remove the other; clear battlefield lists on round end.
acceptance_criteria: After several rounds with sends, duelMatchState battlefield creep lists do not grow unbounded; leak counting unchanged; simulation test asserts cleanup.
close_reason: Battlefield lists reconciled at wave start; escaped creeps pruned; 419 tests green

Player/opponent logic is duplicated across 12+ symmetric method pairs (activeCreeps/opponentCreeps, updateX/updateOpponentX). Extract a Battlefield abstraction instantiated twice and reduce GameScene to orchestration.

title: Extract Battlefield abstraction for player and opponent

acceptance_criteria: One code path serves both battlefields; opponent view switch works as before; tests green.

title: Epic: Placeholder art pipeline
description: Any tower or creep without real art renders an obvious question-mark placeholder instead of crashing or rendering nothing. This unblocks shipping new tower archetypes and creatures before their sprites exist, and makes dropping in the final artwork a registry edit rather than a code change.
design: The placeholder texture is generated procedurally with Phaser Graphics at scene start, so it needs no asset file and matches the existing spritesheet frame contract.
acceptance_criteria: A missing sprite key never throws and never renders an invisible entity; the placeholder is visually unmistakable and race-tinted; replacing it with real art requires only an asset registry entry; a dev-only report lists every sprite key still falling back; the flow is documented.

title: Generate a procedural question-mark placeholder texture
description: Create the placeholder art at runtime with Phaser Graphics: a flat plate with a bold question mark and a dashed border, generated once per scene into a texture that matches the existing spritesheet frame contract so animation code can address frames without special cases. Support a race tint so a placeholder undead tower reads differently from an elf one.
acceptance_criteria: No asset file is required; the texture is generated once and reused; it is legible at tower and creep display sizes on a 360px wide viewport; a test asserts the texture is registered after scene create.

title: Add a sprite resolver with placeholder fallback for units and towers
description: Today spriteKey values like tower.undead.plague and unit.human.footman point at nothing and the sprite factory silently relies on whatever Phaser does with a missing key. Add one resolver used by both the unit and tower sprite factories that returns the real texture when registered and the placeholder otherwise, applying the race tint.
acceptance_criteria: Every sprite creation path goes through the resolver; a missing key never throws and never yields an invisible sprite; the resolver is unit-testable without a live scene; smoke test covers a creep and a tower with unmapped keys.

title: Add a placeholder icon for HUD build buttons and panels

acceptance_criteria: The chip uses design tokens with no magic colours, meets WCAG AA contrast, keeps 44x44 targets, and is covered by a component test asserting no console errors.

title: Report sprite keys that fall back to placeholder art
description: Collect every sprite key resolved to the placeholder and expose the list through the shared logging entrypoint in development only, so it is obvious which art is still missing after adding content. Production builds must not pay for the collection.
acceptance_criteria: The report lists each missing key once with the content id that referenced it; nothing is logged in production; a test covers report contents for a known-missing key.

title: Document the art drop-in flow for new towers and creeps

Extend docs/08-content-authoring.md rather than creating a second page.

Make faction selection actually switch unit rosters, sprites and tileset.

close_reason: Faction rosters wired, tier-based sprite fallback with faction tints, opponent creep sprites fixed

title: Epic: Tower archetypes and race-specific towers
description: Turn the two hardcoded tower types (archer, splash) into data-driven archetypes that can carry on-hit effects, and give every race its own tower roster. Adds frost, poison, chain-lightning and support archetypes on top of the existing single-target and splash ones, so build decisions become tactical instead of cosmetic.
design: Depends on the effect engine for on-hit behaviour and on the content loader from the creature-stats epic. Bridge types stay typed: tower ids are derived from content, never raw strings.
acceptance_criteria: Tower stats, costs, upgrades and on-hit effects come from validated content; the archer/splash union no longer exists in gameplay code; each race has a distinct buildable roster; the HUD build bar is generated from the selected race; the computer opponent handles the new archetypes; a scene test covers build, attack and effect application.

title: Move tower stats and rosters into validated content
description: Author towers as content the same way creatures are: src/content/towers/<race>.json with id, name, race, archetype, costGold, damage, range, attackCooldownMs, splashRadius, onHitEffects and spriteKey. Reuse the validators from the creature content loader. Replace the buildableTowers array and TOWER_COMBAT_STATS_BY_TYPE record.
acceptance_criteria: No tower stat literals remain in src/entities/tower/model/config; content validation reports the offending file and tower id; existing towers keep their current numbers so the change is behaviour-neutral; tests cover loading and validation.

title: Drive tower upgrades from content per archetype
description: TOWER_UPGRADE_CONFIG is a hand-written record keyed by archer and splash, with duplicated arithmetic per level. Move upgrade curves into tower content so each tower declares its own level costs and stat deltas, including effect magnitudes for the new archetypes.
acceptance_criteria: Upgrading any tower reads content only; max level and costs are per tower, not global; the existing upgrade tests are updated and pass; refunds and sell value stay consistent with the new costs.

title: Teach the computer opponent to value the new archetypes
description: scoreTowerPlacement and planBuildDecision assume damage-only towers. Give the opponent archetype-aware weights so it mixes crowd control with damage, respects the roster of its own race, and does not spend everything on support towers.
acceptance_criteria: Difficulty presets still produce distinguishable opponents; the opponent builds at least one crowd-control tower in a simulated ten-wave run at normal difficulty; decision snapshots are updated; simulation tests pass deterministically.

title: Replace the archer and splash union with data-driven archetype ids
description: TowerTypeId, HudTowerType and the build-mode state are hardcoded to archer and splash, and gameSceneBuildRuntime types its parameters as the literal union. Introduce an archetype id derived from content (single, splash, frost, poison, chain, support) plus buildable tower ids, and thread them through the bridge command map without widening anything to plain string.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a tower type across React and Phaser stays typed end to end; no literal archer or splash comparisons remain in runtime code; bridge tests cover the widened command payload; existing gameplay is unchanged.

title: Add the frost archetype that chills its targets
description: First archetype built on the effect engine: a single-target tower with reduced damage that applies chill on hit. Includes its content entry, the on-hit wiring in the combat runtime, a cold projectile tint and its upgrade curve (stronger slow, not just more damage).
acceptance_criteria: Creeps hit by the frost tower slow down visibly and recover after the duration; the slow does not stack into a permanent freeze; damage, cost and slow magnitude live in content; a scene test covers build, fire and slow applied.

title: Add the poison archetype with stacking damage over time
description: A low-direct-damage tower that applies stacking poison, rewarding early placement against long waves. Includes content, on-hit wiring, a green projectile treatment and an upgrade curve that raises stack cap and tick damage.
acceptance_criteria: Poison stacks up to its cap and refreshes duration per the declared stacking rule; a creep killed by poison awards gold once; stats live in content; covered by a scene test.

title: Add the chain-lightning archetype that bounces between creeps
description: An archetype that hits a primary target then jumps to nearby creeps with falloff damage, giving a third answer to grouped waves alongside splash and poison. Bounce count, jump range and falloff come from content; the visual is a chained segment effect rather than a travelling projectile.
acceptance_criteria: Bounces never revisit the same creep within one shot; bounce resolution is deterministic given the same battlefield state; the effect is capped so a dense wave cannot spike the frame budget; unit tests cover target chain selection.

title: Add the support archetype with a nearby-tower aura
description: A tower that deals no damage itself and instead buffs towers in radius (attack speed or range, declared in content). Introduces aura recalculation on build, sell and upgrade rather than per frame, and a visible radius indicator when the tower is selected.
acceptance_criteria: Auras recompute only on battlefield changes, never each frame; buffs stack per the declared rule and are removed when the support tower is sold; selling and rebuilding leaves no stale buff; covered by unit tests.

title: Author race-specific tower rosters for all four races
description: Every race currently has one or two near-identical towers. Give each a roster of four that expresses the race: undead plague and frost wyrm nest, orc lightning totem and burning pit, human cannon bastion and guard post, elf moonwell chill and thorn poison. Update raceRegistries buildableTowerIds and starterTowerId accordingly.
acceptance_criteria: Each race has at least one damage, one crowd-control and one area tower; costs are internally consistent across races; every roster entry resolves to loaded content; race registry tests cover the new ids.

title: Generate the HUD build bar from the selected race roster
description: HudPanel hardcodes two buttons labelled Archer and Plague. Build the bar from the selected race roster with cost, archetype icon and a short effect hint, keeping 44x44 minimum targets, horizontal scroll on 360x800, and no per-frame React updates.
acceptance_criteria: Switching race swaps the buildable set; buttons show cost and disable when unaffordable; verified on 360x800 and 390x844 portrait; HudPanel tests cover the generated list and assert no console errors.

title: Show tower effects in the selected-tower panel
description: The selected tower snapshot carries only damage, range, cooldown and splash radius. Extend it with archetype and on-hit effect summaries (slow percentage, poison per second, bounce count) and render them in TowerActionPanel so the player can compare towers before upgrading.
acceptance_criteria: The bridge snapshot stays typed; the panel renders effect lines only when present; upgrade preview shows the effect delta for the next level; covered by panel tests.

title: Add basic mobile viewport scaling
Epic: Core gameplay loop stabilization
Remove orphaned UI preset assets
description: After the procedural redesign of the pre-game screens (tower-def-a7c), divider.png, panel_frame.png and title_crest.png in src/assets/ui-presets are referenced nowhere. Delete them once the redesign has been reviewed visually; git history keeps the originals. The remaining presets are still used by the in-game HUD widgets.
acceptance_criteria: Unused files removed, build clean, in-game HUD unchanged.
close_reason: All ui-presets PNGs unreferenced after the redesign and deleted; build and tests clean

title: Epic: Visual and mobile polish
description: The game is functional but visually rough and drifts from its own AGENTS.md policy: only 1 of 11 CSS files is a CSS Module, shared/constants/theme does not exist, colors hardcoded in HudPanel.tsx, ~420px of stacked absolute-positioned overlay panels crush the playfield on 360x800, two competing scale systems (Phaser Scale.NONE + manual zoom vs ResizeObserver resize), two independent audio systems (App.tsx new Audio() map vs GameAudioManager).
acceptance_criteria: Playfield clearly visible on 360x800 and 390x844 with panels not overlapping; styles use CSS Modules + theme tokens; one scaling system; one audio system respecting settings volume.
close_reason: All visual/mobile polish tasks done: tokens+modules, layout, scaling, audio

title: Introduce theme tokens and migrate styles to CSS Modules
description: Create shared/constants/theme with color/spacing/typography tokens (AGENTS.md requires it; today only ~77 lines in app/styles/global.css and hardcoded hexes like #5c8cff in HudPanel.tsx). Convert the 10 global CSS files to CSS Modules using the tokens.
acceptance_criteria: No hardcoded colors in TSX; all widget styles are *.module.css; visual parity.
close_reason: Tokens in :root + theme constants; 4 widgets on CSS Modules; no hex in TSX

title: Fix mobile layout: free the playfield from overlay stack
description: GamePage.css stacks absolutely-positioned panels with magic --hud-stack-space: 250px + --creep-send-stack-space: 170px (~420px overlay on an 800px screen) while game-canvas-shell has margin-bottom: 96px and aspect-ratio 2/3. Redesign layout (collapsible/tabbed bottom panels or flex column) so the maze is readable on 360x800.
acceptance_criteria: On 360x800 and 390x844 the full grid is visible and tap targets stay >=44px; panels never overlap the canvas.
close_reason: Flex column layout, canvas free of overlay stack, verified on 360x800/390x844 in browser

title: Unify canvas scaling into one system
description: Phaser.Scale.NONE + manual camera.setZoom in applyResponsiveCamera() conflicts with GameCanvas calling game.scale.resize from a ResizeObserver. Pick one scaling strategy (likely Phaser Scale.FIT or single resize handler driving zoom) and delete the other.
acceptance_criteria: No double-resize artifacts on rotation/resize; playfield centered at correct zoom on mobile and desktop.
close_reason: Single scaling pipeline (Scale.RESIZE + camera refit), verified live in browser

title: Unify audio into GameAudioManager
description: App.tsx keeps its own map of 40 SoundId -> ~15 wav files played via new Audio(), parallel to Phaser GameAudioManager; settings volume only affects the React side. Route all UI sounds through one manager honoring settings volume; dedupe the SoundId->file map.
acceptance_criteria: One audio pipeline; volume setting affects every sound; no duplicate SoundId mappings.
close_reason: Shared audio settings store; settings volume affects game audio; sound map deduplicated

title: Add range indicator when placing towers
description: When user hovers over a cell during build phase, show a visual indicator of the tower's attack range radius. This helps players understand the tower's coverage area before placing. Should render a semi-transparent circle around the hovered cell showing the range in cells based on selected tower type.

title: Force wave start button - ensure prominent visibility
description: Ensure the Force Start Wave button is clearly visible and accessible in the HUD at all times during build phase. The current implementation shows the button correctly but ensure it's always prominent and not hidden by auto-start timer.

title: Fix wave queue display - use animated sprites instead of static images
description: Current wave queue displays static placeholders. Replace with proper animated sprites that match the actual creep types. Make the display smoother with better transitions when creeps spawn and move through the wave.

title: Add a scene-level test harness for GameScene
description: Both high-severity bugs found by the post-refactor review (send queue wiped every build frame, opponent field rebuilt on every view toggle) lived in GameScene and were invisible to 465 tests, because the scene itself has no harness. Build a headless fake-Phaser harness that can drive create/update ticks over the runtime modules and assert duel state transitions.
acceptance_criteria: A test can start a match, queue a send, tick frames, start a wave and assert the send reached the opponent; the two fixed regressions are covered.

Set work to in_progress

title: Epic: Project setup
Downscale oversized UI preset PNGs
description: src/assets/ui-presets holds 10MB of decorative PNGs at ~1400x500 (btn_gray_normal 1.23MB, icon_frame_square 1.54MB, title_crest 1.03MB, ...) used as border-image slices at 10-24px border widths and as center/contain backgrounds - roughly 15x oversampled for a mobile-first game with a 60fps budget. Downscale by 4x and divide border-image slice values (90/85/80) accordingly.
acceptance_criteria: ui-presets total well under 1MB; menus and HUD frames still render correctly; production build succeeds.

title: Create Phaser GameScene with 10x15 debug grid
Fix ambient fade interrupted by route change
description: App.tsx fades the menu ambient out over 220ms with an interval that restores the original volume only when the fade completes. Navigating again mid-fade clears the interval, leaving ambient.volume at the faded-down value permanently.
acceptance_criteria: Ambient returns to the configured volume after any interrupted fade.

title: Per-faction creep art
description: Only undead spritesheets exist. getSpriteKeyByUnit falls back to undead sheets by tier and paints a faction tint (UNIT_FACTION_TINTS), so orc, human and elf creeps are recoloured skeletons.
acceptance_criteria: Each faction has its own creep sprites and walk animations; the tint fallback is removed or kept only for missing tiers.

title: Define shared grid model and cell types
Player send queue wiped every frame in build phase
description: GameScene.applyWaveCompletionRewardIfResolved cleared player.sendQueue and opponent.sendQueue on every frame where canPerformBuildActions() is true - the exact window in which the player can queue sends. Sends were destroyed within one frame: gold spent, income gained, but no creeps ever reached the opponent. The AI was unaffected because it fills its queue synchronously right before routing.
acceptance_criteria: Fixed and verified
close_reason: Send queues cleared at wave start instead of per build-phase frame
